transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-11-12
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus O'Neill (Redwood SE), Priya Menon (HelioHealth CTO), Ahmed Khan (Platform Eng), Sofia Martinez (Security Architect), Diego Ramos (SRE)

Summary: Weekly pilot sync for HelioHealth private deployment. Main items: network routing anomalies after kernel upgrade, fallback policy tuning, telemetry gaps, and next steps for a controlled rollforward and bench tests.

---- Transcript ----
00:00 Lena (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for making time, um, quick agenda — kernel fallout, routing fallbacks, telemetry gaps, and next steps. Marcus will lead the deep part.
00:22 Marcus (Redwood SE): cool. quick recap: on tuesday's kernel push we saw an increase in p95 and some outliers at p99 for short sequences. the thing that stood out was KV cache churn — the cache miss rate spiked when we had an egress route flap.
00:45 Priya (HelioHealth - CTO): yeah, uh, that aligns with what we saw, the long tails were mostly inner-city, sorry, internal API calls that hit the dedicated pool. Diego, do you have the numbers?
00:58 Diego (SRE): yeah so baseline p95 was 38ms, after the upgrade some pods hit 220-450ms at p99, mostly when the request bounced to the fallback model which was on a different AZ and had slightly different quantisization, oh — quantization profile.
01:20 Ahmed (Platform Eng): small correction: the fallback was actually a lighter model in a different region, not simply AZ. egress path took a different hop so serialization latencies added up.
01:34 Marcus (SE): right which suggests two interacting issues: kernel-level scheduling changes increasing tail latency, and smart-routing causing cross-regional fallbacks instead of local model variants.
01:47 Sofia (Security Architect): quick sec — any of this change our data residency / encryption behavior? we need to confirm that fallback routing never crosses regulatory boundaries.
01:58 Lena (AE): good call, Sofia. it's part of our checklist — Redwood policy pins region constraints for fallbacks unless explicitly allowed. we'll re-emit the policy that was in the pilot config.
02:10 Ahmed: can you also confirm audit log entries when a fallback happens? right now we have gaps in the tracing.
02:20 Marcus: logs exist at the control plane, but the pilot's telemetry aggregation missed some events because the sidecar dropped spans during the kernel scheduling pause. we think traces were buffered but not flushed.
02:36 Priya: that buffering is risky for us during a compliance demo, so what's the remediation?
02:41 Marcus: immediate: increase sidecar flush frequency and add a small async write buffer; medium: kernel rollback/patch with targeted scheduler config; longer: root-cause fix with kernel patch from the infra team.
02:58 Diego: on the networking side, we've seen an MTU mismatch on a specific transit link — 1500 vs 9000 — which caused fragmentation and extra CPU on the host, amplifying the latency.
03:14 Marcus: ah yes, MTU mismatch will amplify serialization overhead. can you share the egress firewall and path info?
03:22 Diego: I'll send the ACLs after the call.
03:26 Lena: thank you. next, the rollforward plan — Marcus?
03:30 Marcus: proposed approach: two-step canary. first patch: revert scheduler flags to previous values and enable an experiment toggle in the serving runtime for continuous batching knobs. run for 6 hours on 10% of traffic; monitor p50/p95/p99 and KV miss. if stable, expand to 50% then 100%. if not, immediate rollback using the playbook we'll produce.
03:53 Priya: timeline? we need to align with our security window on monday night.
03:58 Marcus: we can target monday 02:00-06:00 UTC for the 10% canary, followed by bench test on thursday.
04:08 Sofia: for the security window, we need the rollback playbook and signed approvals. Diego will also need to validate the KMS calls during fallback.
04:18 Diego: noted. I need the exact sequence of steps to execute a rollback, including the endpoint calls you said earlier.
04:25 Marcus: okay, that's action item one — produce a step-by-step rollback playbook with API calls, CLI commands, expected outputs, and a fail-safe to pin to previous model version.
04:36 Lena: I'll own follow-up with pricing and pilot hours for the extended bench.
04:41 Priya: question on fallback routing — is it possible to prefer local quantized variants before cross-region fallbacks? we saw quality variance when the fallback was different quant profile.
04:55 Marcus: yes, it's policy driven. we can change the routing table to prefer same-region compatible variants. caveat: this may increase cost if local variants are heavier. we can add a cost cap and a circuit-breaker.
05:12 Ahmed: are cost caps token-based? we need per-route budgeting in our billing export.
05:20 Lena: we can provide route-level cost metrics; exportable to your billing system. Marcus will attach an export template.
05:28 Marcus: will do. also, note that switching to local variants will improve latency but could increase GPU utilization — which might reduce headroom for burst capacity.
05:40 Priya: acceptable as long as we don't degrade overall throughput — we need SLOs to hold.
05:47 Marcus: agreed, we'll run the bench to validate throughput under local-variant routing.
05:52 Sofia: security follow-ups: we need confirmation on SSO/SAML flow for the private control plane and how RBAC maps to our IdP. also request a copy of your SOC 2 self-assessment and encryption diagram.
06:08 Lena: I'll send the SOC 2 docs and the SSO mapping reference. Redwood control plane supports SAML and SCIM provisioning; we'll include examples.
06:18 Sofia: also KMS integration — do you support customer-managed keys or HSM?
06:22 Marcus: yes, we support KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and HSM via our enterprise package for Private. will note the flow in the security pack.
06:34 Priya: on telemetry, you mentioned missing spans — what's your retention and how do we get immutable audit logs for a window?
06:44 Marcus: audit logs are available for export; retention depends on plan. for the pilot we can enable 90-day retention in the private stack, and we can ship compressed event sets to your SIEM via S3 forwarding.
06:58 Diego: perfect.
07:02 Ahmed: bench testing — you mentioned quantization v3. what's different this time?
07:08 Marcus: v3 reduces memory footprint and has a more conservative per-token accuracy profile; it's slightly faster for small sequence workloads, which is our current hot path. but we need to validate output quality against your prompt sets.
07:22 Lena: schedule: bench next Thursday for two hours; we'll run a traffic replay and compare p50/p95/p99 and unit cost.
07:31 Priya: who owns the prompt set? we have a redacted set we can share.
07:35 Ahmed: I'll sanitize a set and upload to the shared drive.
07:40 Marcus: we'll run the bench with and without KV prefix caching to see delta.
07:46 Priya: can we also test with the sidecar flush tweak you mentioned?
07:49 Marcus: yes, that'll be part of the bench matrix.
07:53 Diego: small note: our network team needs MTU guidance. can you provide recommended MTU and a minimal packet size plan?
07:59 Marcus: recommended is 9000 for bulk, but if you can't, ensure consistent 1500 everywhere — inconsistent MTU is the issue here.
08:08 Sofia: on compliance, we need an explicit statement that fallback events are logged with user/anonymized ids before they leave region.
08:16 Lena: yes we'll provide a fallback audit log example showing pseudonymized user IDs and region stamps.
08:22 Priya: ok let's recap and next steps.
08:26 Lena: recap: Marcus to produce rollback playbook and bench script; Marcus to attach telemetry export template; Diego to share ACLs and MTU; Lena to send SOC2 and pricing; Ahmed to upload prompt set; schedule bench for next Thursday.
08:44 Priya: good — any blockers?
08:46 Marcus: the only blocker is the kernel patch acceptance if the canary shows instability; we need signoff for the security window.
08:54 Priya: we'll aim to signoff. Diego will run pre-checks.
08:58 Lena: thanks everyone. I'll send notes and the action items right after.
09:02 [meeting ends]
